info.name: MiddleBy Product Catalog API
info.description:
Requests mirroring Modules/ImportMiddleBy/app/Services/MiddleByApiClient.php.

Setup:
1. Fill in `sub_key`, `client_id`, `client_secret` — take them from the project `.env` (MIDDLE_BY_*). Do NOT use the values from `.env.example`, they point at a different host and return 401.
2. Run "1. Generate token" once — the post-response script stores `token` automatically.
3. Run any other request.

Token lifetime is returned in `expiresOn`; the app refreshes it 60s before expiry. Re-run request 1 when you get 401.

The API rate-limits with HTTP 429. The app retries 3 times with a 2s pause; Postman does not — just wait and retry.

request.description: MiddleByApiClient::getToken(). Returns accessToken + expiresOn. The post-response script saves the token into the collection variable.

MiddleByApiClient::getProduct().

X-Locale and X-Channel are required — they are part of authHeaders() in the client, and the response can differ without them.

Response is ~60-70 KB. Useful things to look for:
- `attributeGroup` — the group an attribute belongs to (e.g. warranty_and_disclaimers_attribute_group, weights_dimensions_attribute_group)
- `"attribute": "url"` — media and document URLs (PhotoFeature / PhotoAlt / VideoFeature / specsheets / usermanuals / brochure / warrantysheet)

MiddleByApiClient::getProductsList() / getProductMiddleByUuid().

This is exactly how the app resolves an AutoQuotes product to a MiddleBy uuid: first by `identifier` + `brand`, and if that misses, by `model` + `brand` with disambiguation on dimensions.

Operators seen in the codebase:
- `iseq` — case-insensitive equality
- `nemp` — field is not empty (used with value "")

Returns `{ data: [ { uuid, identifier, brand, ... } ] }`.

Paginate with `offset` / `limit` to walk a brand. Brand names must match the MiddleBy side of `autoquote_to_middleby_brands` (e.g. "Blodgett", "Imperial", "BKI", "Anets"), not the AutoQuotes vendor name.
